title: Mirza Ghasemi
subtitle: smoky aubergine with eggs
excerpt: Mirza Ghasemi is a northern Iranian dish of charred aubergine mashed with garlic, turmeric and tomato then finished with eggs. The smoky flavour comes from charring the aubergines directly over a flame. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Mirza Ghasemi comes from the Gilan province on the Caspian coast of Iran. It is named after a nineteenth-century governor of the region and has been a fixture of northern Iranian cooking ever since.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smoky northern Iranian dish of charred aubergine cooked with garlic, tomato and eggs, eaten as a dip or main course.

content.text: relies entirely on properly charred aubergines. The skin must be completely blackened over a direct flame or under a very hot grill. The smoky flavour that permeates the flesh cannot be replicated any other way. Serves 4.
Serve as a dip with flatbread, or as a light main course with rice and a simple salad. The eggs are stirred in gently and cooked until just set.

items.prepNote: or 3 fresh tomatoes, peeled and roughly chopped

content.text: Char the aubergines directly over a gas flame, turning with tongs every 3 to 4 minutes, until the skin is completely black and the aubergine feels completely soft when pressed. This takes 15 to 20 minutes. Alternatively, place under the hottest grill setting and turn every 5 minutes.

Place the charred aubergines in a colander over the sink. Leave to cool for 10 minutes then peel off and discard all the charred skin. Chop the flesh roughly and squeeze out any excess liquid. A little char marks on the flesh are fine and add flavour.

Heat the vegetable oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 2 minutes until pale golden and fragrant. Add the turmeric and stir for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the tomatoes have broken down.
Add the chopped aubergine to the pan. Stir and mash together with the tomato mixture. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes until well combined and most of the moisture has cooked off.

Pour the beaten eggs over the aubergine mixture. Stir slowly and continuously until the eggs are just cooked through and custardy, about 3 minutes. Do not overcook. Remove from the heat and drizzle with olive oil. Serve immediately.

attrs.solution: The aubergines must be charred until completely black on the outside. If you do not have a gas hob, a grill on maximum heat works, but takes longer. The smoky flavour only develops when the skin is fully burnt.
After peeling, squeeze the aubergine flesh firmly and leave it in the colander for a few minutes. Cook the aubergine in the pan for longer before adding the eggs to drive off excess moisture.
The eggs should be stirred in over low-medium heat and removed from the heat while still looking slightly underdone. They continue cooking from residual heat.

content.text: Mirza Ghasemi belongs to the Gilan province on Iran's Caspian coast. The region is green, humid and wet compared to the rest of Iran. Its cooking is distinct from the central Persian tradition. Rice, fish, herbs and aubergines dominate. This dish is served warm as a mezze, often alongside other dips. It is widely popular across northern Iran and has spread to the rest of the country.
